findings.summary: The chapter's turn was deleted: the gift-or-prison question and the who-controls-it answer.

evidence.baseline: And here is the turn on which this entire chapter rests. The thing that makes the deep version unacceptable is not the depth of the signal. It is the architecture. A system that fuses every signal of a life is a gift or a prison depending entirely on a single question: who controls it?
evidence.shipped: Such a system could be useful. It could also become the most intimate surveillance device a person has ever invited into their life. Running it locally changes the risk, but does not abolish it.

findings.diagnosis: The shipped section keeps the danger and drops the turn, which is the sentence the whole chapter rests on by its own declaration. Without it the openness argument in the following sections has no hinge. Restored in full with the display line.

findings.summary: The shipped motive bound and restraint drafting are preserved.

evidence.baseline: This is the reason the great technology companies... have not built it. It is not that they lack the capability. It is that the privacy implications are, in their current architectures, catastrophic.
evidence.shipped: The manuscript cannot claim to know why any company has or has not built this particular combination without evidence. ... It should process only what a person deliberately enables, identify and protect the rights of other speakers, use short retention by default, separate functions that do not need to share data, and make deletion intelligible.

findings.authorizedBy: Preservation under CTD-0024 and R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT recording; the motive bound actually lives in chapter twenty's shipped text and is quoted here because it names this section's claim.
findings.diagnosis: The baseline asserts corporate motive (they see the value, they refrain because privacy is catastrophic), which is an unfalsifiable reading of other minds, and the shipped texts bounded it. The bound is not kept in prose because the baseline's claim is the chapter's premise and cutting it is a doctrine change; instead the exposure is recorded and the bound preserved. The bystander-rights restraint drafting (other speakers' rights, short retention, intelligible deletion) is real product canon for CTD-0024's paydown.
